admin.title: Administration
admin.overview.emptyText: Your role lets you make changes in the administration but not open any of its sections. Ask an owner for read access.
admin.forbidden.title: No access
admin.forbidden.text: Only server admins and organization admins can open the administration.
admin.forbidden.section: You do not have the permission this section needs. Ask an admin of your organization if you need it.
admin.members.title: Members
admin.members.lead: People in this organization and their roles.
admin.members.emailHint: The person needs an account on this server. A server admin creates accounts under Users.
admin.members.removeText: Remove {name} from this organization? They lose access to its dashboards and data sources at once. Their account stays.
admin.members.lastOwner: This is the last owner of the organization. Make another member an owner first; an organization always needs one.
admin.members.cannotGrant: You cannot give a role with permissions you do not have yourself.
admin.members.noAccount: No account uses this email address. A server admin can create one under Users.
admin.members.alreadyMember: This person is already a member.
admin.teams.title: Teams
admin.teams.lead: Groups of members that receive roles and access together.
admin.teams.name: Team name
admin.teams.nameTaken: A team with this name already exists. Choose another name.
admin.teams.empty: No teams yet. Teams let you give several members the same roles and access at once.
admin.teams.deleteText: Delete the team “{name}”? Its members lose the roles and access they had through it. Their accounts and memberships stay.
admin.teams.transferTo: Hand its team spaces, folders and dashboards to
admin.teams.transferRequired: Choose who takes over the team’s spaces, folders and dashboards.
admin.teams.transferToOrg: The organization (only admins and grants reach team-only content)
admin.teams.transferHint: Nothing the team owns is deleted with it.
admin.teams.noMembers: This team has no members yet.
admin.teams.everyoneIn: Every member of the organization is already in this team.
admin.teams.removeMemberText: Remove {name} from “{team}”? They keep their own role in the organization.
admin.teams.teamRoleHint: Maintainers can add and remove members of this team.
admin.teams.rolesLead: Every member of the team gets the permissions of these roles, on top of their own role. At most {count} roles; the owner role cannot be given to a team.
admin.teams.rolesChanged: The roles of the team were changed.
admin.roles.title: Roles
admin.roles.lead: Sets of permissions. The built-in roles are fixed; your own roles combine permissions as you need them.
admin.roles.builtinReadOnly: Built-in roles cannot be changed. Create your own role to combine permissions differently.
admin.roles.name: Name
admin.roles.nameTaken: A role with this name already exists. Choose another name.
admin.roles.nameBuiltin: The names owner, admin, editor and viewer are reserved for the built-in roles Owner, Admin, Editor and Viewer. Choose another name.
admin.roles.nameNotAllowed: This name belongs to a built-in role or is not allowed. Choose another name.
admin.roles.notHeld: You can only give permissions you have yourself.
admin.roles.cannotGrant: You cannot give permissions you do not have yourself.
admin.roles.unknownPermission: A permission this version of the interface does not know yet.
admin.roles.notFound: This role does not exist. It may have been deleted.
admin.roles.deleteText: Delete the role “{name}”? Members and teams that have it lose its permissions.
admin.roles.inUse: This role is still given to members. Give them another role first.
admin.permission.dashboards.read: Open dashboards and see their panels.
admin.permission.dashboards.share: Give users and teams of this organization access to dashboards.
admin.permission.folders.read: See folders and what is in them.
admin.permission.folders.permissions: Decide who may access a folder, including restricted folders.
admin.permission.datasources.query: Run own queries on data sources, for example in Explore.
admin.permission.datasources.read: See data sources and their settings, without secrets.
admin.permission.datasources.write: Add data sources and change their connection settings.
admin.permission.datasources.permissions: Decide who may query or change a data source.
admin.permission.annotations.write: Add notes to points in time on dashboards.
admin.permission.teams.read: See teams and who is in them.
admin.permission.teams.write: Create, rename and delete teams and give them roles.
admin.permission.teams.members: Add members to teams and remove them.
admin.permission.users.read: See the members of the organization, for example to share a dashboard.
admin.permission.users.write: Change the role of members and remove them.
admin.permission.roles.write: Create, change and delete own roles.
admin.permission.serviceaccounts.write: Manage service accounts and their tokens.
admin.permission.audit.read: Read the audit log of the organization.
admin.permission.plugins.configure: Configure the plugins a server admin installed.
admin.permission.settings.read: See the settings of the organization.
admin.permission.settings.write: Change the settings of the organization.
admin.permission.org.delete: Delete the organization with everything in it.
admin.access.title: Access to “{name}”
admin.access.lead.folder: Who may use this folder beyond their role. Access to a folder also applies to its subfolders and dashboards.
admin.access.lead.dashboard: Who may use this dashboard beyond their role.
admin.access.lead.datasource: Who may query or change this data source beyond their role.
admin.access.none: Nobody has extra access. Everyone uses the permissions of their role.
admin.access.cannotPick: You may not see users, teams or roles, so you cannot pick whom to give access.
admin.why.buttonLabel: Why do I have this permission? {permission}
admin.why.title: Where this permission comes from
admin.why.none: You do not have this permission.
admin.settings.empty: There are no settings here yet.
admin.settings.notEditable: This setting cannot be changed here.
admin.settings.noWritePermission: You can see this setting, but not change it.
admin.conflict.title: Changed in the meantime
admin.conflict.text: Someone else saved “{name}” while you were editing the setting. Keep their value, or overwrite it with yours.
admin.orgSettings.title: Organization settings
admin.orgSettings.lead: Settings for everyone in this organization. Changes apply at once.
admin.audit.title: Audit log
admin.audit.lead: Who changed what and when in this organization.
admin.users.title: Users
admin.users.lead: Every account on this server, across organizations.
admin.users.name: Name
admin.users.emailTaken: An account with this email address already exists.
admin.users.locked: {name} is locked and can no longer sign in.
admin.users.removedAdmin: {name} is no longer a server admin.
admin.users.lastServerAdmin: This is the last server admin. Make another user a server admin first; the server always needs one.
admin.orgs.title: Organizations
admin.orgs.name: Organization name
admin.orgs.ownerHint: The first owner manages the new organization. Server admins are not members of every organization.
admin.serverSettings.title: Server settings
admin.serverSettings.lead: Settings for the whole server. Values from the environment or the configuration file take precedence and are shown read-only.
admin.serverSettings.fromEnv: Set by an environment variable on the server. Change it there and restart Kalzit.
admin.serverSettings.fromFile: Set in the configuration file kalzit.toml. Change it there and restart Kalzit.
admin.serverSettings.fileOnly: Only the configuration file or the environment can change this, so a wrong value here cannot lock everyone out.
admin.serverAudit.title: Server audit log
admin.serverAudit.lead: Who changed what and when on this server, across organizations.
admin.instances.title: Instances
admin.instances.lead: The Kalzit servers on this database, which one leads and how changes reach them.
admin.instances.leader.lease: Another server takes over within {secs} seconds
admin.instances.hint.versions: The servers run different versions ({versions}). Update the remaining servers soon: an older server cannot start again once a newer one changed the database.
admin.instances.hint.postgres: To add a server, start Kalzit on another machine with the same database and the same secrets key behind your load balancer. The leader runs the jobs that must run once; if it stops, another server takes over.
admin.instances.hint.sqlite: SQLite serves one Kalzit server. To run several servers behind a load balancer, move to PostgreSQL.
admin.account.title: Your account
admin.account.lead: Your name, password, sessions and permissions.
admin.account.name: Name
admin.account.emailHint: A server admin can change it.
admin.account.passwordLead: Changing the password signs you out everywhere else; this browser stays signed in.
admin.account.currentWrong: The current password is not correct.
admin.account.sessionsLead: Browsers where you are signed in.
admin.account.revokeOthersText: End all other sessions? Those browsers have to sign in again.
admin.account.permissionsLead: In {org} you are {role}. What you may do there:
admin.account.noPermissions: You have no permissions in this organization.
admin.common.changedMeanwhile: Not undone: someone else changed this in the meantime. The page now shows the current state.
admin.members.exceedsYou: You can only change or remove members, and give roles, whose permissions you hold yourself.
admin.members.aboveYou: This member’s role has permissions you do not have, so you cannot change or remove them.
admin.members.unknownRole: This role does not exist anymore. Reload the page and choose another.
admin.teams.rolesInvalid: The server did not accept these roles. A team can have at most 20 roles, and never the owner role.
admin.teams.rolesExceedYou: This team’s roles have permissions you do not have, so you cannot change the team or its members.
admin.teams.rolesAboveYou: The team’s roles have permissions you do not have, so you cannot add or remove its members.
admin.teams.rolesRestored: The roles of the team were restored.
admin.roles.limit: This organization already has the most custom roles it can have. Delete one before creating another.
admin.roles.limitReached: This organization has {count} custom roles, the most it can have.
admin.roles.aboveYou: This role has permissions you do not have, so you cannot change or delete it.
admin.roles.ownerOnly: Only the built-in owner role has this.
admin.access.cannotGrant: You can only give access up to what you may do on this yourself.
admin.access.cannotSee: You cannot see who has access to this. Ask someone who manages its access.
admin.settings.rejected: The server did not accept this value. Check it and try again.
admin.audit.toBeforeFrom: Choose an end date on or after the start date.
admin.why.grantAbove: Access “{level}” on a folder above, given to {subject}
admin.users.lockText: Lock {name}? They are signed out everywhere at once and cannot sign in until you unlock them.
admin.users.demoteSelfText: You lose access to the server administration at once and cannot undo this yourself. Another server admin has to give the role back.
admin.users.setPasswordText: The user is signed out everywhere and signs in with the new password.
admin.orgs.ownerGone: This account does not exist anymore. Choose another owner.
admin.orgs.noOwner: There is no account that can sign in to own the organization. Create or unlock a user first.
admin.auditAction.datasource.deleted: Data source moved to the trash
admin.users.cannotLock: This account cannot be locked: it is the last server admin, or the last owner of an organization who can sign in. Give that role to someone else first.
admin.settings.datasources.sqlite_dirs.d: Folders on the server from which SQLite data sources may open database files. The data folder is always refused. If the list is empty, no SQLite files are allowed.
admin.settings.datasources.file_dirs.lab: Folders for CSV and JSON files
admin.settings.datasources.file_dirs.des: Folders on the server from which file data sources may read CSV, JSON and NDJSON files. The data folder is always refused. If the list is empty, no files are allowed.
admin.settings.datasources.allowed_targe: If this list is not empty, data sources may only connect to these hosts and networks.
admin.settings.datasources.query_timeout: How long a single query may run before it is stopped.
admin.settings.datasources.max_rows.desc: The most rows, points, documents or nodes a single query returns.
admin.settings.datasources.max_response_: How much memory the results of one request may take, with all its queries together. Counted as held in memory (every value, text and document entry), which is more than the JSON text.
admin.settings.datasources.max_parallel_: How many queries run at once on the whole server. Further ones wait for a free slot, at most until their time limit runs out.
admin.settings.datasources.max_inflight_: How much memory the results of all running queries may take together.
admin.settings.datasources.cache_enabled: Keeps answers of queries for the time each data source sets, per person, so a dashboard that is opened or refreshed again does not ask the database again. Off, nothing is kept.
admin.settings.datasources.cache_max_byt: How much memory the kept answers may take together; the ones used least recently go first.
admin.settings.ai.enabled.label: AI functions
admin.settings.ai.enabled.description: Turns every AI function on or off. Off, the UI shows no AI buttons or hints.
admin.settings.ai.request_timeout_secs.d: How long a single call to the AI provider may take, including the streamed answer.
AI calls per user and day
How many AI calls a user may make per day (UTC) in one organization; 0 means no limit.
admin.settings.ai.user_tokens_per_day.la: AI tokens per user and day
admin.settings.ai.user_tokens_per_day.de: How many tokens (input and output) a user may use per day (UTC) in one organization; 0 means no limit.
admin.settings.ai.org_tokens_per_month.l: AI tokens per organization and month
admin.settings.ai.org_tokens_per_month.d: How many tokens all members of an organization may use together per calendar month (UTC); then AI is refused there until the month ends. 0 means no limit.
admin.settings.ai.max_rows_to_model.desc: The most rows, documents or nodes of a result the AI receives; more are cut off with a note.
admin.settings.ai.max_tool_calls.label: Tool calls per answer
admin.settings.ai.max_tool_calls.descrip: The most tool calls the assistant makes for one answer in “Ask”; then it answers with what it has.
admin.settings.ai.allow_org_providers.de: Organization admins may connect their own AI provider with their own key. The server’s limits still apply.
admin.settings.ai.org_enabled.label: AI in this organization
admin.settings.ai.org_enabled.descriptio: Off means no AI buttons and no “Ask” for members of this organization, even while AI is on for the server.
admin.settings.ai.max_concurrent.label: AI calls at once
admin.settings.ai.max_concurrent.descrip: How many AI calls may run at once on the whole server; a further one is refused until one ends.
admin.settings.ai.max_concurrent_per_org: AI calls at once per organization
How many AI calls all members of an organization may have running at once together.
admin.settings.ai.max_concurrent_per_use: AI calls at once per user
How many AI calls one user may have running at once.
admin.settings.ai.chat_retention_days.de: AI chats are deleted this many days after their last message; 0 keeps no chats. Organizations can only choose a shorter time. Applies once chats are stored.
admin.settings.ai.notice_text.label: AI notice addition
admin.settings.ai.notice_text.descriptio: A paragraph of your own under the notice about which data leaves the server, which everyone sees before their first AI call.
admin.settings.audit.retention_days.desc: Audit events are deleted after this many days, since they can hold client addresses.
admin.settings.usage.enabled.label: Record usage
admin.settings.usage.enabled.description: Counts dashboard views and panel and data source queries for Administration > Usage, per dashboard, panel and data source only, never per person. Applies at once.
admin.settings.usage.retention_days.desc: Usage counts are deleted after this many days, at most 90.
admin.settings.appearance.default_langua: Language of the UI for users who have not chosen one.
Theme of the UI for users who have not chosen one.
admin.settings.sessions.lifetime_hours.d: A session ends this many hours after sign-in.
admin.settings.sessions.idle_timeout_hou: A session ends after this many hours without a request. 0 means never.
admin.settings.dashboards.version_retent: Versions kept per dashboard; older ones are deleted on save. 0 keeps all.
admin.settings.dashboards.default_time_r: Time range of new dashboards in this organization.
admin.settings.dashboards.new_in_team_sp: New dashboards in the team space
New dashboards go into the team space of the team a member works in.
admin.settings.appearance.product_name.d: Shown in the sidebar, on the sign-in page and in the browser tab.
admin.settings.appearance.accent.label: Accent color
admin.settings.appearance.accent.descrip: For primary actions only; the contrast is checked.
admin.settings.appearance.density.label: Density
admin.settings.appearance.density.descri: Spacing in lists, panels and forms.
admin.settings.appearance.font_size.desc: Size of body text; headings, controls and spacing grow with it.
admin.settings.appearance.start_page.des: Where members land after signing in when they have no start dashboard of their own.
admin.settings.appearance.time_zone.desc: For everyone who has not chosen one. Times in dashboards and lists use it.
admin.settings.appearance.week_start.des: For calendars and ranges like “this week”, for everyone who has not chosen one.
admin.settings.signin.welcome.label: Sign-in welcome text
admin.settings.signin.welcome.descriptio: Replaces the line under the heading of the sign-in page.
admin.settings.signin.notice.label: Sign-in notice
admin.settings.signin.notice.description: Shown above the sign-in form, such as privacy or a maintenance window.
admin.settings.server.http_addr.label: HTTP address
admin.settings.server.http_addr.descript: Address and port of the plain HTTP listener; empty turns it off.
admin.settings.server.https_addr.label: HTTPS address
admin.settings.server.https_addr.descrip: Address and port of the HTTPS listener; empty turns it off.
admin.settings.server.public_url.label: Public URL
admin.settings.server.public_url.descrip: The address users open. The origin check and links use it.
admin.settings.server.redirect_http_to_h: With HTTPS on, plain HTTP answers with a redirect.
admin.settings.tls.cert_file.label: Certificate file
admin.settings.tls.cert_file.description: Certificate chain of the HTTPS listener, as PEM. It is reloaded without a restart.
admin.settings.tls.min_version.label: Minimum TLS version
admin.settings.tls.min_version.descripti: The oldest TLS version HTTPS accepts.
How often the certificate files are checked for changes. 0 means never.
Reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded headers are believed. Everyone else’s are ignored.
admin.settings.security.hsts.label: HSTS
admin.settings.security.hsts.description: Tells browsers to use only HTTPS for this server.
admin.settings.security.hsts_max_age_sec: How long browsers keep to HTTPS after a visit.
admin.settings.security.login_max_failur: Per email address and per client address; further attempts wait until the window ends.
admin.settings.security.two_factor_requi: The minimum for every organization. Whoever has none sets one up at the next sign-in; organizations may only be stricter.
admin.settings.security.two_factor_metho: What people may set up. Recovery codes always come with them.
admin.settings.security.login_window_sec: The time in which failed sign-ins are counted.
admin.settings.security.setup_max_failur: From all client addresses together while Kalzit is not set up; beyond it every check waits until the window ends.
admin.settings.security.setup_window_sec: The time in which wrong setup codes from all addresses are counted.
admin.settings.log.level.label: Log level
admin.settings.log.level.description: Which messages the server writes, such as info or kalzit=debug,info.
admin.settings.log.format.label: Log format
admin.settings.log.format.description: Text for people, JSON for log collectors.
admin.updates.title: Updates
admin.updates.lead: Update Kalzit online or install a signed package offline. A backup is made before every update.
admin.updates.channel.previewHint: Previews before each release, for trying new features
admin.updates.autoCheck.on: Daily, never installs on its own
admin.updates.window.zone: Time zone {zone} · planned updates run only in this window
admin.updates.window.title: Maintenance window
admin.updates.window.text: Planned updates start at the beginning of the window. If the server is not running then, the update waits until you plan it again.
admin.updates.upToDateText: Version {version} is the newest of its channel.
admin.updates.upToDateNever: Check for updates, or upload a package below.
admin.updates.noKey: This build trusts no release key, so it cannot verify updates. Install a build of a release.
admin.updates.mode.windowsService: Kalzit does not run as its Windows service, so it cannot restart itself.
admin.updates.mode.notSystemd: This server was not started by systemd, so Kalzit cannot restart itself.
admin.updates.mode.binaryNotWritable: The service account may not replace the Kalzit binary.
admin.updates.mode.container: Kalzit runs in a container: update the image instead.
admin.updates.mode.cluster: Other Kalzit servers use the same database, so this one does not install on its own. Update the servers one after the other.
admin.updates.mode.unsupported: This system cannot install updates on its own.
admin.updates.mode.command: The release is downloaded and verified. Stop Kalzit, run this command as an administrator, then start Kalzit again:
admin.updates.pre.title: Before the update
admin.updates.pre.backupPostgresHint: Kalzit cannot back up a PostgreSQL database; use pg_dump before you install.
admin.updates.pre.users: Active users in the last 30 minutes: {count}
admin.updates.pre.usersHint: They see a short interruption while Kalzit restarts.
admin.updates.pre.restartHint: If the new version is not healthy within {seconds} s, Kalzit returns to {version} on its own.
admin.updates.restartingWait: Kalzit is restarting with {version}. This page reconnects on its own.
admin.updates.offline.title: Offline update
admin.updates.offline.lead: For servers without internet access: download the package, carry it over and upload it here.
admin.updates.offline.step1Hint: For Windows x64 or Linux x64
admin.updates.offline.step2Hint: Ed25519 against the built-in key; the version must be newer
admin.updates.offline.step3Hint: Now or in the maintenance window, with a backup
admin.updates.offline.where: Packages are on the GitHub releases of MouseWerk/Kalzit.
admin.updates.offline.verified: The package is verified and ready to install.
admin.updates.backups.title: Backups
admin.updates.backups.none: No backups yet. Kalzit makes one before every update.
admin.updates.backups.postgres: Kalzit keeps no backups of a PostgreSQL database; back it up with your own tools.
admin.updates.backups.foot: Older backups are removed automatically. They contain password hashes and encrypted secrets: keep downloads safe.
admin.updates.history.title: History
admin.updates.history.manualReturn: To return to a kept version here, stop Kalzit and run kalzit update rollback with the version.
admin.updates.confirm.installText: Kalzit makes a backup, replaces itself and restarts. If the new version is not healthy within {seconds} s, it returns to {version} on its own.
admin.updates.confirm.postgres: I backed up the PostgreSQL database with pg_dump.
admin.updates.confirm.returnText: Kalzit replaces itself with the kept {version} and restarts. Your data stays as it is.
admin.updates.confirm.returnRestore: The database changed since {version}. Returning puts back the backup taken when {version} was left: everything changed since then is lost.
admin.settings.updates.channel.label: Update channel
admin.settings.updates.channel.descripti: Which releases updates offer: stable releases only, or previews too.
admin.settings.updates.check_daily.label: Check for updates daily
admin.settings.updates.check_daily.descr: Ask GitHub once a day whether a new version exists. Nothing else is sent, and nothing installs on its own.
admin.settings.updates.window.label: Maintenance window
admin.settings.updates.window.descriptio: When planned updates run, as HH:MM-HH:MM in your local time.
admin.settings.updates.keep_versions.des: Previous versions kept with their database backups, for a return.
admin.settings.updates.health_timeout_se: How long a new version has to report healthy before Kalzit returns to the previous one.
admin.settings.plugins.catalog_enabled.d: Load the signed plugin catalog. Off, Kalzit makes no connection for it; installing from a file always works.
admin.settings.plugins.catalog_url.label: Plugin catalog address
admin.settings.plugins.catalog_url.descr: HTTPS address of the catalog list; its signature is read from the same address with .sig appended.
admin.settings.plugins.catalog_refresh_h: How often the catalog list is loaded again while the catalog is on.
admin.settings.ai.provider_explain.label: Provider for explain and draft
admin.settings.ai.provider_explain.descr: The server’s provider for “Explain” and “Draft”; empty uses the default provider. An organization’s own provider comes first.
admin.settings.ai.provider_summarize.des: The server’s provider for “Summarize”; empty uses the default provider.
admin.settings.ai.provider_chat.label: Provider for Ask (chat with tools)
admin.settings.ai.provider_chat.descript: The server’s provider for “Ask”; empty uses the default provider.
admin.updates.mode.deb: Kalzit was installed from the deb package, so apt updates it: download the new release’s deb and install it with this command.
admin.updates.mode.rpm: Kalzit was installed from the rpm package, so dnf updates it: download the new release’s rpm and install it with this command.
admin.invitations.title: Open invitations
admin.invitations.lead: Links work for 7 days and once.
admin.invitations.revokeText: The link to {email} no longer works afterwards.
admin.invitations.resent: New link sent to {email}; the old one no longer works.
admin.invitations.emailsHint: Separate several with a comma, a space or Enter.
admin.invitations.emailsRequired: Enter at least one email address.
admin.invitations.publicUrlMissing: Links need the public address of the server: server.public_url in kalzit.toml or KALZIT_SERVER_PUBLIC_URL.
admin.invitations.roleGone: The role of this invitation is gone. Revoke it and invite again.
admin.invitations.expiredCopy: The invitation has expired; send it again.
admin.invitations.linkUnavailable: The link cannot be shown any more; send the invitation again.
admin.invitations.createdText: No mail server is set up. Send the link yourself, in a chat for example. It works until {date}, and only once.
admin.invitations.laterNote: You can copy the link again later under Open invitations.
admin.members.passwordLinkNoMail: This server does not send mail. A server admin can set a new password under Users.
admin.members.passwordLinkElsewhere: This account signs in without a password of its own in Kalzit.
admin.account.unconfirmed: This address is not confirmed yet: the account came from an invitation link that was passed on. Until it is confirmed, nobody can add you to another organization by this address.
admin.account.confirmSent: Link sent to {email}. It works for 24 hours.
admin.account.confirmNoMail: This server does not send mail; the address cannot be confirmed now.
admin.members.unconfirmed: This account has not confirmed its email address yet. Invite the person or ask them to confirm the address under Profile.
